title: Skeletons and Muscles
seo_title: Year 3 Science: Skeletons and Muscles Worksheets (Bones, Joints and Muscles)
standard_text: Identify that humans and some other animals have skeletons and muscles for support, protection and movement.
meta_desc: Free Year 3 science worksheets on skeletons and muscles: the main bones, support, protection and movement, muscles working in pairs, and animal skeletons. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Muscles pull on bones; they work in pairs.
body_html:
How to think about it

A skeleton supports the body, protects organs and helps it move.

  • The skull protects the brain; the ribs protect the heart and lungs; the spine holds us upright.
  • Muscles pull on bones by contracting. They work in pairs, like the biceps and triceps.
  • Some animals have a skeleton inside, some have a hard skeleton outside, and some have none.
Example

Which bone protects the brain?

Head

Answer: the skull

Example

Bending the arm: which muscle contracts?

Front of the upper arm

Answer: the biceps

Common mistakes

  • Thinking muscles push bones.
  • Thinking bones are not alive.
  • Thinking all animals have a skeleton like ours.

faq.a: It supports the body and gives it shape, protects soft organs such as the brain, heart and lungs, and works with muscles so we can move.
A muscle contracts (gets shorter) and pulls on a bone. Muscles work in pairs: when the biceps pulls the arm up, the triceps relaxes, and the triceps pulls it straight again.

faq.q: Do all animals have a skeleton?
faq.a: No. Vertebrates such as humans, fish and birds have bones inside. Insects, spiders and crabs have a hard outer skeleton. Worms, slugs and jellyfish have no skeleton.
